message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a range of distinctive physical and chemical properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average; varies with isotope) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (120.65 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g/L at 25 °C (gas) |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L/mol (ideal gas at STP) |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; reacts explosively with air in a wide concentration range (4–75 % H₂ in air). |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H, D), Tritium (^3H, T). |
| **Bonding characteristics** | Forms covalent bonds; typically forms diatomic molecules (H₂). In compounds, it often acts as an oxidizing agent (e.g., H₂O, H₂SO₄). |
| **Solubility in water** | Low (~1.6 g/100 mL at 25 °C) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive with many elements; forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). |
| **Spectral lines** | Prominent Balmer series in visible spectrum; Lyman series in ultraviolet. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), industrial processes (ammonia synthesis via Haber process), rocket propellant, laboratory reagent. |

These properties make hydrogen unique among elements, influencing its role in chemistry, physics, and technology.
